help.title: How to use this page
help.intro: Run a Python snippet against your data and see whatever it print()s — quick stats, grouping, exports, anything pandas can do.
help.step1: Pick the data — Grid data uses every row currently in the Query tab's table (query result or uploaded file); Snapshot data runs against a stored snapshot instead.
help.step2: Write Python — your rows arrive in a variable named data (a list of dicts, one per row). pandas is pre-installed: import pandas as pd.
help.step3: Run script — the output panel shows what the script printed (errors included). Files the script saves land in your Downloads folder — see the Excel example.
help.step4: Reuse — Insert example loads ready-made snippets, Use template / View opens the shared template library, and Save + Custom keep your own scripts one click away.
help.tipTitle: Tip — let Copilot (or any AI) write the script for you
help.tipIntro: Ask an external LLM such as GitHub Copilot Chat or ChatGPT, and give it three things:
help.tipTask: the task you want done — e.g. “top 10 HOLD_CODEs by row count”,
help.tipContract: the contract — rows come in data (a list of dicts), pandas is available, results are shown via print(),
help.tipSample: a sample of your data — copy a few rows from the grid and paste them in.
help.tipOutro: The prompt below already covers the contract — fill in the task and paste your sample rows:
help.copilotPrompt:
Write a Python 3 script for the ODBC Query App "Script" tab.

Contract:
- My query result is already loaded in a variable called data — a list of dicts, one dict per row, e.g. [{'LOT_ID': 'A123', 'QTY': 10}, ...].
- pandas is available (import pandas as pd). Built-ins like math/json are fine.
- Show every result with print() — that output is exactly what the app displays.
- Use plain Python/pandas only; do not install packages, open dialogs, or touch the database.

Task: <describe what you want, e.g. "count rows per HOLD_CODE, sort by count, show the top 10">

My data (columns plus a few sample rows, copied from the grid):
<paste a handful of rows here>
